title: The first World Championship
text: On 13 May 1950 Silverstone hosts the first round of the new FIA World Championship. Giuseppe Farina wins in an Alfa Romeo 158 and goes on to become Formula 1's first World Champion.

title: The Fangio era
text: Juan Manuel Fangio wins five titles in seven seasons with four different manufacturers — Alfa Romeo, Mercedes, Ferrari and Maserati. His record of five championships stands for 46 years.

title: A title for the teams
text: The Constructors' Championship is introduced, rewarding the car builders as well as the drivers. Vanwall wins the first one.

title: Engines move to the back
text: Jack Brabham takes the title in a rear-engined Cooper. Within two seasons almost every team has copied the layout, which F1 cars still use today.

title: The monocoque
text: Colin Chapman's Lotus 25 replaces the old tube frame with a stiff, light monocoque chassis. Jim Clark uses it to win the 1963 title.

title: Cosworth, wings and sponsors
text: The Ford Cosworth DFV engine wins on its debut in the Lotus 49 and goes on to power cars for 15 years. In 1968 teams adopt sponsor liveries and the first wings appear.

title: The turbo arrives
text: Renault enters with the turbocharged RS01. It is fragile at first, but by the early 1980s turbo engines are producing well over 1,000 horsepower in qualifying.

title: Ground effect
text: The Lotus 79 uses shaped underfloor tunnels to suck the car to the track. Mario Andretti wins the title, and every team rushes to copy the idea.

title: McLaren's perfect season (almost)
text: Ayrton Senna and Alain Prost win 15 of 16 races in the McLaren MP4/4. Their rivalry defines the sport for the next few years.

title: Imola and a safety revolution
text: Roland Ratzenberger and Ayrton Senna are killed at the San Marino Grand Prix. The tragedy drives sweeping changes to car design, circuits and medical care that have saved many lives since.

title: Schumacher and Ferrari
text: Michael Schumacher wins five titles in a row with Ferrari, taking his total to a then-record seven championships and 91 wins.

title: The Brawn fairytale
text: Rescued from Honda's withdrawal weeks before the season, Brawn GP wins both championships with Jenson Button in its only year of existence.

title: Vettel and Red Bull
text: Sebastian Vettel becomes the youngest World Champion and wins four titles in a row with Red Bull Racing.

title: The hybrid era
text: 1.6-litre V6 turbo-hybrid power units arrive. Mercedes masters them first and wins eight Constructors' titles in a row; Lewis Hamilton equals Schumacher's record of seven championships in 2020.

title: The halo
text: The titanium halo becomes mandatory to protect drivers' heads. Initially controversial, it is credited with saving several drivers in serious crashes.

title: A final-lap title
text: Max Verstappen beats Lewis Hamilton to the championship on the last lap of the season in Abu Dhabi, after a year-long duel.

title: Ground effect returns
text: New rules bring back underfloor aerodynamics to help cars follow each other closely and make overtaking easier.

title: Record-breaking dominance
text: Verstappen wins 19 of 22 races — the most in a single season — on his way to a third straight title.

title: Norris takes the crown
text: Lando Norris wins his first World Championship after a season-long fight with McLaren teammate Oscar Piastri.

title: A new era
text: The biggest rule change in a decade: smaller, lighter cars with active aerodynamics, power units with a near 50/50 split between combustion and electric power, and 100% sustainable fuel. Audi and Cadillac join to make an 11-team grid.
